chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani informed us from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, on the authority of his father, who said: 'I heard Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) say'
Whoever asks God for forgiveness seventy times during the month of Sha'ban, God will forgive his sins even if they are as numerous as the stars.

key_terms.شَعْبَانَ: The eighth month of the Islamic lunar calendar

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for seeking forgiveness seventy times in the month of Sha'ban?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (peace be upon him) narrates that seeking forgiveness (istighfar) seventy times during the month of Sha'ban results in the forgiveness of one's sins, even if they are as numerous as the stars. This tradition, recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, underscores the unique spiritual status of Sha'ban in Shia tradition as a month of divine mercy and preparation for Ramadan. The specific number 'seventy' is often interpreted by scholars as a complete or perfect count, emphasizing the thoroughness of repentance required to attain such vast forgiveness.
